messages:
sanjay: Bringing up Avalanche15b (int4) on pool-az1. After ~48h of traffic we saw 2 burst OOMs when clients use max_new_tokens > 128. Not a steady leak, looks like fragmentation/cold-start spikes. Anyone run into this with large int4 models?

ellie: hmm, fragmentation on int4 is common at warmup. Are these requests high-context or lots of diverse session lengths? Also: are we using prefix cache + aggressive prefetch?

mike: logs from the node:
```
[2026-03-23T15:03:11Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-23T15:03:11Z] slab: freelist after alloc: 3.2MB (was 12.8MB)
[2026-03-23T15:03:11Z] kv_cache: entries=42, hit_rate=0.12
```
Requests that OOMed had max_new_tokens 256 and varied prefix lengths (avg 900 tokens).

lee: that slab flip looks like rapid churn in allocation sizes. Two quick mitigations: lower per-route default max_new_tokens to 128, and reduce aggressive prefetch slots for this model. Also consider enabling soft-throttle when estimated total_seq > 1024.

sanjay: good call. Want to try a canary: per-route override + prefetch slot reserve change. I can roll to 2 nodes in az1. @mike can you add the log hooks to capture slab freelist histograms?

mike: done — added a 30s histogram dump on the canary. Also I reproduced locally with the curl below and saw same OOM in ~200 requests:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"avalanche15b-int4\",\"input\":\"<long chat>\",\"max_new_tokens\":256,\"temperature\":0.0}'
```

ellie: config snippet I'd try for canary (console/manifest):
```
{
  \"model\":\"avalanche15b-int4\",
  \"defaults\":{
    \"max_new_tokens\":128,
    \"batch_window_ms\":12,
    \"prefetch_slots\":2,
    \"kv_cache_prefetch\":false
  },
  \"slo_guards\":{
    \"soft_throttle_tokens\":512
  }
}
```
This keeps batching but reduces speculative allocations.

lee: alternative experiment: disable continuous batching for the canary workloads for 1h to see if fragmentation still spikes. If it doesn't, points to batching fragmenting the slab.

sanjay: rolling the manifest to pool-az1/canary-2 now. applying per-route and prefetch changes. tagging rollout with canary id c-20260323-1.

deploy-bot: Canary c-20260323-1 applied to pool-az1 (2 nodes). Observability: latency and slab histograms enabled.

mike: after 2k requests on canary (mixed clients): 0 OOMs so far. Latency +12-18ms p95. Slab histograms show fewer small free fragments, freelist stable at ~11MB median.

ellie: promising. If canary holds for 6h, propose making the per-route default 128 for avalanche15b across dedicated pool and add a graceful fallback: if request.max_new_tokens > 128 and pool free_mem < 20% then reject with 429 + guidance to reduce max_new_tokens.

sanjay: agree. I'll file a short runbook for on-call: what to do if we see repeated OOMs after rollout (rollback manifest, pin to float variant, escalate to infra).

lee: long-term: we should benchmark kernel affinity and small-allocation caching for int4 -- might need a per-model allocator config. Filing a tech task: MLINFRA-872 (alloc tunables for int4 models).

mike: TL;DR: immediate fix = canary with max_new_tokens default 128 + prefetch_slots=2. Monitoring: slab histograms, kv hit rate, OOM count.

sanjay: thanks all — I'll update the model onboarding checklist to include a frag/slot sanity test and a max_new_tokens recommendation. :thumbsup:
